characterization_methods.key_findings: Initial structure = large polygonal grains with strong parallel segregation striations (Fig. 1). After deformation the DRX degree ranks large deformation zone (3) > small deformation zone (2) > difficult deformation zone (1); DRX volume fraction and grain size increase with temperature and with decreasing strain rate. For the present condition (1150 °C, 10 s⁻¹) the DRX average grain size is ~20–25 µm (Fig. 10/11a).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis; after sample preparation, grinding, polishing and etching; etching solution 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction); fields carry a 100 µm scale bar.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the initial and hot-deformed microstructures in the three deformation zones of the compressed sample and measure the DRX average grain size.

characterization_methods.key_findings: Provides the flow-stress curves, peak stress and characteristic values used to derive the DRX activation energy, Z parameter and DRX grain-size models.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 1150 °C, 10 s⁻¹, to 60% height reduction (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricant on end faces; water-spray quench after deformation.
characterization_methods.purpose: Acquire flow-stress (rheological) data and produce hot-deformed microstructures for DRX analysis.
characterization_methods.technique: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression testing (thermo-mechanical simulation)

analytical_models.equation_role: Characterizes the combined influence of temperature and strain rate on the flow stress / DRX behaviour
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ increases with increasing strain rate and decreasing temperature (Table 1); for this sample (1150 °C, 10 s⁻¹) lnZ = 58.92, the lowest value among the 10 s⁻¹ series.

analytical_models.equation_role: ε̇ = A[sinh(ασp)]^n·exp(-Qp/RT); used to determine the DRX activation energy
analytical_models.model_note: Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2 (formula 2). The activation energy is a material constant derived from the whole experimental matrix, not from this single condition.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: T = 900–1150 °C, ε̇ = 0.01–10 s⁻¹, peak stress σp data over the full experimental matrix.
computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine constitutive analysis (linear regression of ln ε̇–ln[sinh(ασp)] and ln[sinh(ασp)]–1000/T)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The parallelism of the fitted lines in Fig. 4 is not good, so the calculated Q is only the average value within the experimental range.

analytical_models.equation_role: Predict εc, σc, εp, σp, εs, σs as functions of lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Models derived by multiple linear regression over the full T/ε̇ matrix; apply to the material including this sample's condition.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Critical strain from θ–σ inflection point (Poliak–Jonas criterion); material constant C from ln(σ/σp) vs [ln(ε/εp)+1−ε/εp] fit
computational_details.simulation_method: Multiple linear regression of flow-curve characteristic values (εc, σc, εp, σp, εs, σs) against lnZ; critical strain from Cingara-McQueen equation
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: εc/εp ≈ 0.452, consistent with literature values; fit quality R = 0.911–0.957 (Fig. 6).

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts the DRX average grain size d_rex as a function of strain rate and temperature
analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model
analytical_models.model_note: Initial grain size and strain were taken as fixed values (a·d0^h·ε^p regarded as a constant); model built with the Levenberg–Marquardt optimization algorithm.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as rigid-plastic body; die indenter as rigid body; material parameters given to the die; semi-symmetric specimen model to shorten simulation time; friction of the billet–die contact interface set to shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient of billet and air set to 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation in line with the thermal-compression experimental conditions.
computational_details.simulation_method: Finite-element simulation plus Levenberg–Marquardt mathematical regression for a DRX average grain-size prediction model
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: R = 0.996; MRE for all samples = 4.53%; absolute error between predicted and experimental grain size mostly within 3 µm.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sample heated from room temperature to 1200 °C at 10 °C/s (part of the shared thermo-mechanical schedule).
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature 1150 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held 15 s at 1150 °C so that the temperature difference between inside and outside of the sample was the same.

Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression at a strain rate of 10 s⁻¹ to 60% height reduction (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricant were affixed to both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
Immediately after compression the sample was water-spray cooled.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression to 60% (maximum true strain 0.92) on a Gleeble-3500 simulator; heated to 1200 °C at 10 °C/s, homogenized 120 s, cooled at 5 °C/s, held 15 s at temperature, then water-spray quenched; mica foils + high-temperature lubricant on both end faces.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Hot-compression true stress–true strain behaviour at 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹: the flow curve rises to a peak stress and then softens to a plateau (DRX-type curve). The exact 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹ curve is only shown within the Fig. 3(d) 3D peak-stress map (strain rate 1–10 s⁻¹, colour bar 94.00–486.0 MPa), which drops sharply as temperature approaches 1150 °C; no explicit single value is printed for this condition.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: large polygonal grains spanning roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar

microstructure_list.region: bulk (as-forged forging billet, before hot compression)

structures.overall_structure: Initial (pre-deformation, as-forged) microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel: large polygonal grains delimited by bright etched boundaries whose dark grey interiors contain abundant fine, closely spaced, parallel light striations, giving a strongly banded dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution.

microstructure_list.region: core of the compressed sample (large deformation zone, zone 3)

structures.overall_structure: Dynamically recrystallized grain structure produced by isothermal hot compression to 60% (true strain 0.92) at 1150 °C and 10 s⁻¹. The paper reports only the DRX average grain size for this condition (measured in the large-deformation zone at the specimen core); no optical micrograph for exactly 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹ is presented (Fig. 9 covers 1150 °C only at 1 s⁻¹).

unmapped_findings: For the present condition (1150 °C, 10 s⁻¹) the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: flow (rheological) stress increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature, so peak stress can be reduced by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (b0012, b0021, b0024, b0084).

High-strain-rate trend relevant to this sample: at the high strain rate 10 s⁻¹ the peak stress decreases by 73% within the 900–1150 °C range (for comparison, at 0.01 s⁻¹ it decreases from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C, an 82% reduction). These are range statements for the 10 s⁻¹ series, not a discrete value for 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹ (b0024).
This sample's lnZ (Table 1, 10 s⁻¹ column, 1150 °C row) = 58.92, the lowest lnZ among the reported conditions; lnZ increases with increasing strain rate and decreasing temperature (table_001, b0037).
The 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹ condition lies outside the fine-and-uniform-grain hot-working windows recommended by the authors: 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s⁻¹ and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s⁻¹ (b0012, b0065, b0086).

No optical micrograph is provided for exactly 1150 °C/10 s⁻¹; Fig. 9 covers 1150 °C only at 1 s⁻¹ (panel f) and 10 s⁻¹ only at 1100 °C (panel c), so the deformed microstructure of this exact sample is only represented through its measured DRX average grain size (~20–25 µm, figure_010/figure_011).

For context (other condition, not this sample): at 1150 °C and 0.01 s⁻¹ the DRX grain size exceeds 70 µm and the structure is coarse-grained, indicating rapid recrystallized-grain growth (b0063, figure_010).

As-forged initial microstructure of the steel shows pronounced banded segregation contrast (fine parallel striations within every grain), i.e. chemical heterogeneity in the as-forged condition (figure_001).

Material-level hot-deformation constants derived from the full experimental matrix (not this single condition): DRX activation energy Qp = 669.844 kJ mol⁻¹; R = 8.314 J/(mol·K); α = 0.00599; k1 = 5.135; k2 = 15.690; C = 0.1461 at 1050 °C/0.01 s⁻¹ (R = 0.9728); εc/εp ≈ 0.452 (b0029, b0032, b0045, b0054, figure_005).
The steel composition (mass fraction, %) is 1.46 C, 25.14 Mn, 10 Al, 0.053 Nb, balance Fe, i.e. the alloy of this sample (b0018).

The experiments were confirmed to be reproducible: isothermal constant-strain-rate compression tests on the same steel batch/composition under identical conditions were used to check the reproducibility of the proposed system, and the reported experimental phenomena have reproducibility (b0018, b0024, b0037, b0058, b0065).
